detail.longDescription: I'm trying to serve a 27B GGUF model on RunPod Serverless with an OpenAI-compatible API, scaling to zero when idle. Setup: Endpoint type: Load Balancer (so I get a real /v1/chat/completions path) Image: ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda GPU: 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 (fallback H100 80 GB) Workers: 0 active, 1 max, idle timeout 300 s Start command: llama-server \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \ -hf <user>/<repo>:<quant> \ -c 262144 \ -ngl 99 \ --flash-attn on \ --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 When I send a request after the endpoint has been idle, a worker starts, but the request fails with: timed out waiting for worker The worker logs show the model downloading and loading normally, and if I keep retrying for a few minutes, a request eventually succeeds and everything works while the worker stays warm. Why does RunPod give up on the worker even though llama-server is starting fine, and how can I make the first request succeed (or at least make cold starts usable)?
